narrative.summary: No AI-specific law has been identified in Cuba so far. A Strategy for the Development and Use of Artificial Intelligence led by the Ministry of Communications was reported approved in 2024 under the Digital Transformation Policy. The personal data protection law, Law 149 of 2022, gives people a right to object to automated profiling that significantly harms their interests.
narrative.review_notes: Not yet verified from the official text: the 2024 AI strategy and the Digital Transformation Policy. The Official Gazette, the National Assembly, the Ministry of Justice, the science ministry and the Central Bank were checked on 18 October 2026, including the official text of Law 149/2022.

instruments.official_title: Ley No. 149 "De Protección de Datos Personales"
instruments.english_title: Law No. 149 on Personal Data Protection
instruments.issuing_authority: National Assembly of People's Power (Asamblea Nacional del Poder Popular)
instruments.publisher_name: National Assembly of People's Power (Asamblea Nacional del Poder Popular)
instruments.current_status: Adopted by the National Assembly of People's Power at its session of 14 May 2022 and published in the Gaceta Oficial, Edición Ordinaria No. 90 of 25 August 2022 (GOC-2022-832-O90). The law states that it enters into force 180 days after its publication in the Gaceta Oficial. The Ministry of Justice is charged with overseeing compliance. The same gazette issue carries Ministry of Communications Resolution 58/2022 on the security of personal data in electronic form (see leads).
instruments.summary: Cuba's personal data protection law. It sets the principles, procedures and definitions for protecting personal data held in physical or digital records and databases, public or private, and regulates processing by public and private persons and entities. Article 23 lets individuals object to processing, automated or not, that significantly harms their interests and is intended to evaluate personal aspects or to analyse or predict matters such as work performance, economic situation, health, reliability or behaviour.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Only general law identified that governs personal-data processing by AI systems in Cuba; it includes a right to object to automated or non-automated profiling-type processing (Article 23.2). No AI-specific law exists.
metadata_gaps: Effective date not printed as a calendar date (law states entry into force 180 days after publication)

instruments.official_title: Ley 182/2025 "General de Ciencia, Tecnología e Innovación"
instruments.english_title: Law No. 182/2025, General Law on Science, Technology and Innovation
instruments.issuing_authority: National Assembly of People's Power (Asamblea Nacional del Poder Popular)
instruments.publisher_name: National Assembly of People's Power (Asamblea Nacional del Poder Popular)
instruments.current_status: Adopted by the National Assembly of People's Power on 18 December 2025 and published in the Gaceta Oficial, Edición Ordinaria No. 94 of 9 November 2026 (GOC-2026-638-O94). Final Provision Four: in force sixty days after publication (computed as 8 January 2027). Its regulation, Decree 154/2026 of the Council of Ministers, is published in the same issue.
instruments.summary: Cuba's general law on science, technology and innovation. Article 8 requires the actors of the science, technology and innovation system to evaluate the ethical implications of their work, in particular of emerging technologies such as genetic engineering, biotechnology, neurotechnologies and artificial intelligence. Article 10 provides for an Artificial Intelligence Ethics Committee, the body that ensures the scientific validity and ethical justification of the use of AI in research, whose members are appointed by the Minister of Communications.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: General law with explicit AI provisions: an ethics-evaluation duty that names AI and an AI Ethics Committee for research.
instruments.evidence_reference: Desktop browser pane, 2026-11-17: Gaceta Oficial issue page No. 94 Ordinaria (Fecha 09/11/2026; Ley 182 de 2025, GOC-2026-638-O94) and the issue PDF read: pp. 3919-3920 Article 8(c) and Article 10.3 (Comité de Ética para la Inteligencia Artificial, members designated by the ministro de Comunicaciones); p. 3942 Disposición Final Cuarta (entra en vigor a los sesenta días posteriores a su publicación) and 'DADA ... a los 18 días del mes de diciembre de 2025'. Decree 154/2026 not checked for AI provisions.

leads.title: Estrategia para el Desarrollo y Uso de la Inteligencia Artificial
leads.english_title: Strategy for the Development and Use of Artificial Intelligence
leads.issuing_authority: Ministry of Communications (MINCOM); approved by the Council of Ministers
leads.note: Ministry of Communications statements say the strategy was approved in May 2024 as part of the Política para la Transformación Digital and presented publicly in January 2025; six axes (ethics and legal framework, human capital, applications and services, public administration, science and innovation, social communication). No official full text or gazette publication found; mincom.gob.cu and gacetaoficial.gob.cu unreachable from the research environment. Record once the official text is located (e.g. mincom.gob.cu/es/print/6983). 2026-10-18: Ministry of Communications site refused access from the research location (access restricted by IP); the Official Gazette keyword search returned no result for 'inteligencia artificial'. Still no official text; kept as lead. 2026-11-07: Ministry of Communications pages now readable: mincom.gob.cu/es/print/6983 states the AI development strategy was approved in May 2024 as part of the Digital Transformation Policy; printpdf/6952 mentions a Consejo Técnico Asesor; printpdf/6652 (Informática 2026) says the Council of Ministers approved the digital transformation policy and refers to the digital agenda to 2030 and the AI development strategy. No full text, number or Official Gazette reference on any page; kept as lead. 2026-11-17: Ministry of Communications and Official Gazette sites still could not be opened; no official text found. Kept as lead.

leads.title: Resolución 58/2022 del Ministro de Comunicaciones (Reglamento para la seguridad de los datos personales en soporte electrónico)
leads.english_title: Ministry of Communications Resolution 58/2022 (Regulation on the security of personal data in electronic form)
leads.note: Implements Law 149/2022 for electronic personal data; PDF at https://www.mincom.gob.cu/sites/default/files/marcoregulatorio/r_58-22_registro_de_base_datos_personales_.pdf (unreachable). Unclear whether it has AI-relevant content; general data-security rule, not recorded. 2026-10-18: official text read in Gaceta Oficial No. 90 Ordinaria of 25 August 2022 (GOC-2022-833-O90, https://www.gacetaoficial.gob.cu/sites/default/files/goc-2022-o90_0.pdf), dated 19 August 2022, entering into force 180 days after publication. It sets security requirements for processing personal data in electronic form, citing the growth of automated processing; no AI-specific provisions. Kept as lead (general data-security rule).

leads.title: Resolución 24/2026 del Ministro de Comunicaciones (metodología para la transformación digital y la introducción de la inteligencia artificial en la Administración Pública)
leads.english_title: Ministry of Communications Resolution 24/2026 (methodology for digital transformation and the introduction of AI in public administration)
leads.note: 2026-11-24: press reports (not official sources) say the resolution was published in the Gaceta Oficial No. 96 Ordinaria of 17 November 2026, signed by the Minister of Communications on 30 October 2026, and enters into force seven days after publication; it reportedly sets a methodology and a roadmap to 2030 (2026-2027 enabling capacities and rules, 2028 pilots, 2029-2030 scaling), requires AI systems used by public bodies to allow audit and control by the State, and makes MINCOM's Directorate General of Informatics responsible for oversight. The Official Gazette and Ministry of Communications sites could not be opened, so the official text, number and dates are not verified. Record once the official text is read on gacetaoficial.gob.cu (expected file goc-2026-o96.pdf).
